_meta.description: Hypothesis register. Each hypothesis states a falsifiable prediction, the exact test executed, and the verbatim evidence returned. 'supported'/'refuted' describe the evidence gathered in this session only.
_meta.reverification_note: 2026-09-17 fifth pass (~20:58Z): H22 (frontier drift is rank-heterogeneous within one interval) and H23 (cash-prize level is reachable only at an unbroken compounded daily rate; ruin arithmetic at 20:1) added and supported on capture 5. H14-H21 unchanged; no verdict changed. All frontier and champion numbers re-derived by scripts/verify.py including the new data/leaderboard_lab.json artifact.

hypotheses.claim: Returns of >=10x on the paper account are achievable in The Leap and have been officially recorded.
hypotheses.prediction: At least one completed edition has a published #1 net profit >= 900%.
hypotheses.test: Count records in data/verified_explosive_returns.json with return_multiple >= 10.
evidence: Completed Futures - February 2025: BenBernanke1, +5,220.72% (53.2072x), 59,187 participants.
Live AMP Futures - September 2026 snapshot: leonardo22_romano, +921.49% (10.2149x), 93,527 displayed participants; in progress and not a final result.

hypotheses.claim: In the captured official champion sample, records at or above 10x occur in futures editions; the two captured stock editions finished below 1.3x.
hypotheses.prediction: At least one completed futures record is at or above 10x, while both captured completed stock records are below 1.3x.
hypotheses.test: Group completed records in data/verified_explosive_returns.json by asset_class_label and compare their observed ranges. Do not infer causation or a universal strategy route.
evidence: Completed futures sample: best 53.2072x and at least one record above 10x.
Completed stocks sample (n=2): 1.299x and 1.1758x.
This small champion-only sample does not prove that leverage or asset class caused the difference.

hypotheses.claim: The live (September 2026) contest permits trading single stocks.
hypotheses.prediction: The permitted instrument list contains at least one NASDAQ/NYSE/AMEX single-stock contract.
hypotheses.test: Parse data/contest_universe.json and count instruments whose exchange is an equity venue.

hypotheses.claim: Per-unit volatility by itself is sufficient to identify the best instrument for absolute-dollar leaderboard placement.
hypotheses.prediction: If sufficient, no position-cap, multiplier, quote-price, or buying-power input would change the dollar P/L comparison.
hypotheses.test: Combine each selected instrument’s rules cap, verified multiplier, captured TradingView continuous-contract price, and the 20:1 initial buying-power limit. Compute whole-contract modeled notional and the favorable percentage move needed to equal the captured rank-250 P/L. Historical normalized volatility is not available, so do not rank expected returns.
evidence: Dollar P/L per underlying point equals contracts × multiplier; dollar P/L for a 1% move also depends on price.
At the captured prices, the 20:1 buying-power model reduces CL from its rules cap of 100 contracts to 48 whole contracts, SI from 25 to 15, HO from 25 to 23, and NQ from 100 to 8.
The favorable underlying moves needed to equal the captured rank-250 P/L are 12.6853% for CL, 12.8094% for SI, 12.9120% for HO, and 13.3236% for NQ under the stated model assumptions.

Conclusion is limited: volatility alone is insufficient. The repository has not measured normalized historical volatility and does not claim that caps, margin, or any one instrument is the binding or best predictor.

hypotheses.claim: The live rules rank participants by realized profit/loss on closed positions, and the public leaderboard displays both percentage and absolute-dollar columns.
hypotheses.prediction: The rules define realized P/L on closed positions as the ranking metric, and displayed dollars are consistent with displayed percentage on the 250,000 virtual-USD base.
hypotheses.test: Read the ranking clause and recompute captured leaderboard rows within the maximum error implied by percentage rounding.
evidence: Rules: 'A participant’s place ... is determined based on the realized profit/loss on the Competition account.'
Rules: realized P/L is P/L on closed positions; all open positions are automatically closed at the end and included.
The leaderboard displays 'Realized profit %' and 'Realized profit $'.
Snapshot rank 1: 250,000 × 9.2149 = 2,303,725, exactly the displayed realized P/L. Closing timing does not create extra P/L; it only changes when open P/L becomes realized.

hypotheses.claim: A return at or above 100x is present in the 16-record official contest sample captured by this repository.
hypotheses.prediction: At least one captured official record shows return_multiple >= 100.
hypotheses.test: Count captured records with return_multiple >= 100.
evidence: 0 cases at or above 100x across all 16 sourced records.
The sample maximum is 53.2072x (Futures - February 2025). This does not prove a universal ceiling or exhaust every edition.

hypotheses.claim: Contest parameters are stable across editions, so a strategy tuned once carries over.
hypotheses.prediction: Balance, leverage, position caps and commission are identical between consecutive futures editions.
hypotheses.test: Diff the TradeStation Jul 2026 rules against the AMP Futures Sep 2026 rules.
evidence: Balance 100,000 -> 250,000 virtual USD (2.5x).
Futures leverage 10:1 -> 20:1 (2x); max notional 1,000,000 -> 5,000,000 (5x).
NYMEX:CL1! position cap 1.0 -> 100.0 contracts (100x).
CME:MBT1! position cap 5.0 -> 25.0 contracts (5x).
Prize-paying ranks 250 -> 300.

hypotheses.claim: A free-plan account can compete on equal terms in the live edition.
hypotheses.prediction: Free-plan participants receive the same market data as paid participants.
hypotheses.test: Read the real-time data clause (section 06) of the live rules.
evidence: Rules: free-plan users 'who were not previously active users of TradingView's paid services will not be provided with the Competition Real-Time Data by reason of their participation in the Competition.'
Rules: after subscribing, 'access to the Competition Real-Time Data will then be granted within twenty-four (24) hours'.
They may register and are prize-eligible, but they trade without competition real-time data unless they subscribe or trial.

hypotheses.claim: The leverage-implied upper bound on initial account notional is $5,000,000 before per-symbol caps and whole-contract constraints.
hypotheses.prediction: The starting balance multiplied by stated futures leverage equals $5,000,000.
hypotheses.test: Recompute starting_balance_virtual_usd × futures_leverage_ratio from the live rules.
evidence: 'The preset balance size for the Paper Trading Competition Account is 250,000 virtual USD. Leverage for futures: 20:1.'
Computed upper bound: 250,000 x 20 = 5,000,000 USD. Actual initial deployment can be lower because of position caps and whole-contract quantities.

Corollary (computed): an adverse move of 250,000 / 5,000,000 = 5.00% on a hypothetical fully deployed $5,000,000 notional equals the entire starting balance. Equivalently 1/20 = 5%, the inverse of the stated leverage.

hypotheses.claim: The captured live leaderboard frontiers are point-in-time values that move during the edition; at 2026-09-16T21:39:34Z, ranks 50, 100, and 250 displayed +457.64%, +384.08%, and +249.48%.
hypotheses.prediction: A later same-day capture can differ from an earlier capture because the rules allow leaderboard updates during the contest.

evidence: Tier boundaries: rank 25 +578.89%, rank 26 +569.30%, rank 50 +457.64%, rank 51 +454.33%.
Earlier same-day archived rank-250 values were lower, demonstrating snapshot drift.
The public page displays only ranks through 250 even though rules award up to 300 potential prizes; no public rank-300 threshold is claimed.

hypotheses.claim: A Donchian channel breakout with EMA-trend and ATR-expansion filters (model S1) earns a positive walk-forward median net profit on daily bars across the capturable contest universe.
hypotheses.prediction: Across non-overlapping 30-day walk-forward windows on every captured symbol with >=150 bars, the pooled median net profit is positive (>$0) at zero cost, survives removal of the best symbol and best window, and nearby channel lengths (15, 25) keep it positive.
hypotheses.test: scripts/run_backtests.py (engine intel-1) simulated S1 on 11 captured symbols (231 windows, 2024-09-17 to 2026-09-17 vendor daily bars, run stamp 2026-09-17T03:15:40+00:00) per research/strategy/testing-plan.md; verdicts follow the pre-registered falsification rules.
evidence: Pooled median net profit at zero cost is $0.0 (mean $11,400.80 is driven by outliers); 14.72% of 231 windows were positive.

Only 74 closed trades total (56 long, 18 short); 3 of 231 windows reached >=5x (best: COMEX:SI1! 2025-12-08->2026-01-06, 7.3872x on a single trade; the other two are NYMEX:CL1! 6.5076x and 7.1851x, also single-trade), 0 reached >=10x.
Concentration checks fail: excluding the best symbol or the best window flips the pooled median non-positive; per-symbol medians are $0.0.
Sensitivity grid (zero cost): channel15 -> 80 trades, 14.72% positive; channel25 -> 74 trades, 14.72% positive; initial fixed sizing -> 74 trades. All medians $0.0.
Adding CME:BTC1! (captured 2026-09-17T03:15:40Z, 504 sessions) did not change the verdict or the set of >=5x windows.

hypotheses.claim: An EMA impulse continuation entry (fast EMA crossing/holding above slow EMA with ATR expansion, model S2) earns a positive walk-forward median net profit on daily bars.
hypotheses.prediction: Pooled median net profit across all captured-symbol walk-forward windows is positive at zero cost and stays positive after moderate costs ($1.50/side + 5% ATR slippage) and at nearby EMA pairs (15x40, 25x60).
hypotheses.test: scripts/run_backtests.py simulated S2 on the same 11 symbols / 231 windows (run stamp 2026-09-17T03:15:40+00:00) with the pre-registered cost and sensitivity protocol.
evidence: Pooled median net profit at zero cost is $0.0 and the mean is negative (-$2,475.13); only 7.36% of 231 windows were positive.
30 closed trades in 231 windows; 0 windows reached >=5x (best window CME_MINI:NQ1! 2025-02-11->2025-03-12 at 1.8722x).
Moderate-cost median $0.0 (mean -$3,376.81); high-cost median $0.0 (mean -$4,275.87).
Sensitivity grid (zero cost): ema15x40 -> median $0.0 (29 trades), ema25x60 -> median $0.0 (38 trades); concentration checks fail on symbol and window removal.

hypotheses.claim: Entering on a Bollinger-band squeeze release (bandwidth at a 50-bar low then expansion, model S3) captures the volatility expansions that follow squeezes, earning a positive walk-forward median net profit on daily bars.
hypotheses.prediction: Pooled median net profit across captured-symbol walk-forward windows is positive at zero cost, and the trade count is large enough for the declared bootstrap confidence interval.
hypotheses.test: scripts/run_backtests.py simulated S3 on the same 11 symbols / 231 windows (run stamp 2026-09-17T03:15:40+00:00); squeeze-release signals on daily bars are rare, so the sample-size rule applies.
evidence: Only 5 closed trades in 231 windows (1.3% of windows positive); the pre-registered rule rejects a bootstrap CI on 5 trades.
Pooled median net profit at zero cost is $0.0 (mean $132.58); 0 windows reached >=5x (best NYMEX:NG1! 2026-06-17->2026-07-16 at 1.158x).
Sensitivity grid (zero cost): band_length 15 -> median $0.0 (5 trades), band_length 25 -> median $0.0 (9 trades).
S3's signal is too rare on daily bars to be a leaderboard strategy inside 30-day windows; intraday data would be required to re-test it meaningfully.

hypotheses.claim: Within the capturable universe, the instruments whose historical 30-day moves most exceed the move needed to match the last publicly visible leaderboard rank (rank 250; cash prizes end at rank 50) are the full-size energy and metals contracts (CL1!, HO1!, RB1!, SI1!, PL1!), because their modeled initial notional hits the leverage cap, while micro contracts and ETH1! are structurally priced out.
hypotheses.prediction: Ranking captured symbols by (best 30-day up move) / (favorable move needed to reach the $623,689 rank-250 target from the modeled initial notional) puts full-size CL/HO/RB/SI/PL at the top, NG1! near the middle despite the highest volatility, and QM1!/ETH1! at the bottom.
hypotheses.test: data/volatility_intelligence.json (written by scripts/run_backtests.py alongside the backtests) computed annualized volatility, ATR(14), best 30-day up/down moves and the rank-250 requirement per symbol from the same vendor daily bars.
evidence: Needed vs delivered (favorable move needed -> best 30d up move, rank-250 target $623,689 from the 2026-09-16 snapshot): CL1! 12.7%->58.4%, HO1! 12.9%->78.2%, SI1! 12.8%->64.7%, RB1! 18.4%->66.7%, PL1! 27.9%->50.3% - each historically delivered 1.8x-6.1x its requirement inside one 30-day window.
NG1! needed 86.3% (margin-limited notional $722,750) and historically delivered 140.4% (ratio 1.63); QM1! (needed 121.8%) and ETH1! (needed 517.7%) are structurally priced out (ratios 0.48 / 0.14).

New in this run: CME:BTC1! (captured 2026-09-17T03:15:40Z) needed 163.9% against a best 30-day up move of 48.8% (ratio 0.30) - its 1-contract cap x multiplier x price leaves a $380,425 modeled notional, far below the rank-250 requirement.
This is simulation arithmetic on vendor data (upper envelope of what history offered), not a forecast and not a backtest of a tradable strategy.

hypotheses.claim: The public leaderboard frontier (ranks 1/50/100/250) of the live AMP Futures September 2026 edition is non-stationary during the contest: by the third capture (~19.5 hours after the first) all four frontier P/L values had risen and three of the four had changed holders.
hypotheses.prediction: Capture 3 (2026-09-17T16:56:00Z) shows strictly higher realized P/L at ranks 1, 50, 100 and 250 than capture 1 (2026-09-16T21:39:34Z).
hypotheses.test: Comparison of capture 1 vs capture 3 in data/frontier_history.json; every value quoted verbatim from the official contest page (evidence TV-CONTEST-AMP-SEP2026.md, TV-CONTEST-AMP-SEP2026-2026-09-17.md, TV-CONTEST-AMP-SEP2026-2026-09-17-R3.md).
evidence: Displayed participants rose 93,527 -> 93,702 -> 95,709 (+2,182 total) over the same window while registration remained open until 2026-09-23 08:00 UTC.

The 3-hour quiet between captures 1 and 2 (rank 1 and 250 frozen) did not generalize: during the US trading day all four frontiers moved up. The P/L required to hold any given public rank is a rising moving target, and no captured value is a final threshold.

hypotheses.claim: The last cash-prize rank (50) sits far above the last publicly visible rank (250): holding rank 50 required roughly 90% more realized P/L than holding rank 250 at the third capture, and the actual last-prize frontier (rank 300) is not observable on the public board.
hypotheses.prediction: At capture 3, (rank-50 P/L - rank-250 P/L) / rank-250 P/L > 0.9.
hypotheses.test: Arithmetic on capture 3 of data/frontier_history.json: (1,247,897.00 - 655,069.50) / 655,069.50; prize tiers from official rules section 09.
evidence: Cash prizes end at rank 50 (ranks 26-50 at $400 each); ranks 51-300 receive 3-month subscriptions (official rules section 09). The public leaderboard exposes only ranks 1-250, so the P/L actually required for rank 300 - the real last prize - is unobservable (IR-06).
Practical reading: a strategy aimed at any cash prize must target well above the rank-250 frontier, and the gap is widening as the contest progresses (H18).

hypotheses.claim: The public live leaderboard is corrected over time, not append-only: between capture 3 (2026-09-17T16:56:00Z) and capture 4 (2026-09-17T19:04:00Z) the displayed rank-50 frontier DECREASED from +$1,247,897.00 to +$1,244,313.50 while ranks 100 and 250 rose and rank 1 was unchanged; the exact row value previously displayed at rank 50 (rajgaurav009 +$1,247,897.00) re-appeared at rank 49.
hypotheses.prediction: Capture 4 rank-50 realized P/L is strictly lower than capture 3 rank-50 realized P/L, and the capture-3 rank-50 row value appears verbatim (same trader, same percentage, same dollars) at rank 49 in capture 4.
hypotheses.test: Row-by-row comparison of captures 3 and 4 in data/frontier_history.json plus the full-board rows 45-116 re-read verbatim from the official contest page (TV-CONTEST-AMP-SEP2026-2026-09-17-R4.md).
evidence: Rank 50: +$1,247,897.00 (+499.16%) -> +$1,244,313.50 (+497.73%): -$3,583.50 (-1.4334 pp); holder changed from rajgaurav009 (now at rank 49 with the identical value pair) to Nikola_Ng.

Realized P/L on closed positions cannot shrink for a still-registered account; the net effect is exactly one fewer row ahead of the tracked row, and the most parsimonious explanation is one removal from the board ranked 1-48 at capture 3 (disqualification or board correction; official rules sections 05, 09 and especially 16 reserve at-any-time disqualification rights and the official pages publish no board-change log).

Control rows behaved normally over the same 2.1-hour window: rank 1 unchanged ($2,335,125.00, same holder), rank 100 +$12,309.65 (new holder JeremyTradezzz; capture-3 holder wowlass63 slid to rank 103), rank 250 +$2,235.50 (new holder NxSChadha).
Consequence for strategy: a captured frontier value is not a ratchet floor; the P/L needed for any rank at contest end cannot be read off as 'minimum observed so far' in either direction.

hypotheses.claim: Every tracked public frontier's average realized-P/L accumulation rate since the competition start is positive and quantified, so a static lead decays: from 2026-09-01T08:00:00Z to capture 4 (2026-09-17T19:04:00Z, 16.4611 days) the displayed frontiers averaged $141,857.07/day (rank 1), $75,591.10/day (rank 50), $61,490.53/day (rank 100) and $39,930.78/day (rank 250).
hypotheses.prediction: Each of the four capture-4 frontier values divided by the 16.4611 elapsed days is positive, and the rank-50 average rate exceeds the rank-250 average rate.
hypotheses.test: Division of capture-4 realized P/L in data/frontier_history.json by elapsed days computed from data/contest_config.json dates; constant-rate scenario = value x (29.1667 total contest days / 16.4611 elapsed days); scenario arithmetic only, not a forecast.
evidence: Average rates over 16.4611 elapsed days: rank 1 $141,857.07/day; rank 50 $75,591.10/day; rank 100 $61,490.53/day; rank 250 $39,930.78/day. All positive; mid-board rates sit far above the board edge, so the gap between cash ranks and the public edge is structural (H19).

Time remaining at capture 4: 12.7056 days to the 2026-09-30 12:00 UTC deadline; registration stays open for 5.5389 more days (until 2026-09-23 08:00 UTC), about 43.6% of the remaining window, so newly joining participants can still push the board upward during that part of it.

Constant-rate scenario values at contest end (arithmetic equalities, NOT forecasts): rank 1 ~$4,137,497.89; rank 50 ~$2,204,740.42; rank 100 ~$1,793,473.89; rank 250 ~$1,164,647.74. H18/H20 show the true path is non-stationary and even correctable downward, so these scenario numbers bound nothing.

Practical reading for a leaderboard-placement attempt: the entry threshold keeps rising on average, so deferring entry raises the required final P/L; the 5 active UTC days qualification can be satisfied any time before the deadline.

hypotheses.claim: Frontier drift is rank-heterogeneous: inside one short interval some tracked ranks can be completely static while others advance, so the displayed board is not one moving level and 'the frontier' has no single rate.
hypotheses.prediction: Between capture 4 (2026-09-17T19:04:00Z) and capture 5 (2026-09-17T20:58:00Z) at least one tracked rank is unchanged to the cent while at least one other tracked rank rises.
hypotheses.test: Diff the four tracked rank values of captures 4 and 5 in data/frontier_history.json and re-identify the displaced rows by their exact displayed values.
evidence: Ranks 1 and 50 byte-identical across the 1.90-hour interval: leonardo22_romano +$2,335,125.00 and Nikola_Ng +$1,244,313.50 (0.00 change), while rank 100 rose +$2,747.50 (JeremyTradezzz +$1,012,202.50 -> nynyyynn54 +$1,014,950.00) and rank 250 rose +$3,454.50 (NxSChadha +$657,305.00 -> mrchrissmithl143 +$660,759.50).

Row identity proves which boundary moved: capture-4's rank-100 row re-appeared verbatim at rank 101 and capture-3's rank-100 row (wowlass63 +$999,892.85) at rank 105, so one new row entered between rank 50 and rank 100 while the cash-prize edge did not move at all.

This is the first observed interval in which the rank-50 cash edge was static while lower tracked frontiers rose; it does not contradict H18/H20, which show the path is non-stationary and even correctable downward, and it means a static edge is not evidence that entry is 'still cheap'.
Practical consequence: any placement plan must be re-priced against the latest capture, not against a single measured rate; the frontier tracker's deltas are the only honest measure of what changed.

hypotheses.claim: The cash-prize level is arithmetically reachable from a fresh account inside the remaining window, but only at a strictly positive compounded daily rate that must hold every day: at capture 5 the rank-50 level is 5.9773x the starting balance, so a new 250,000 account needs +15.2122%/day compounded for the 12.6264 days left, equal to a 0.7606%/day underlying move at the rules' 20:1 leverage.
hypotheses.prediction: Re-deriving from data/contest_config.json and data/frontier_history.json yields a positive required daily compound rate for every tracked rank, and an adverse full-exposure move smaller than 5% of the underlying is enough to erase the entire starting balance.
hypotheses.test: Deterministic arithmetic in scripts/leaderboard_lab.py -> data/leaderboard_lab.json: required daily compound = (balance multiple)^(1/remaining days) - 1; underlying equivalent = rate / 20; ruin arithmetic = 100% / 20x leverage; cross-checked by scripts/verify.py against the capture and config files.
evidence: Required daily compounding from the 2026-09-17T20:58:00Z capture (12.6264 days left): rank 1 +20.3236%/day, rank 50 +15.2122%/day, rank 100 +13.7017%/day, rank 250 +10.7815%/day. Underlying equivalents at 20:1: 1.0162% / 0.7606% / 0.6851% / 0.5391% per day.

Balance-multiple targets over the same window: 5x needs +13.5946%/day (0.6797% underlying), 10x +20.0050%/day (1.0002%), 20x +26.7770%/day (1.3389%), 50x +36.3192%/day (1.8160%), 100x +44.0119%/day (2.2006%); at an illustrative +1% underlying day with full reinvestment, 5x takes 9 unbroken winning days and 100x takes 26.

Exposure arithmetic: maximum initial notional is $5,000,000 (250,000 x 20), so 1% of underlying is $50,000 = 20% of the starting balance; a 2.5% adverse move erases half the balance and a 5% adverse move erases all of it. The rules forbid resetting the account (section 08), so the required path admits no full-exposure loss day.

Reality check from this repository's own tests: the three pre-registered models are refuted with $0.0 pooled median net profit across 231 windows (H14-H16), so no tested strategy has produced any positive daily compounding, let alone the unbroken sequence above. The arithmetic shows what the prize costs; it is not evidence that it can be earned.
Cross-check: the rank-50 level (5.9773x) is above 14 of the 15 completed-edition champion records; only BenBernanke1's 53.2072x is higher (cross-edition context only).
